vedic_reference.note: Sarvadev is a compound name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘सर्व’ meaning ‘all’ and ‘देव’ meaning ‘god’. It is a name for Lord Vishnu, who is considered the Lord of all Gods. Sarvadev is mentioned in various Vedic texts such as the Rigveda and the Bhagavad Gita.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sarvadev holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it represents the belief in a multitude of gods and the supreme God, Lord Shiva. The name reflects the polytheistic nature of Hinduism and highlights the idea of various deities coming together to form a divine entity. It also emphasizes the concept of unity in diversity, as Sarvadev encompasses all other gods.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sarvadev carries deep spiritual significance as it embodies the ultimate truth of Hinduism, which is Shiva as the supreme deity. Sarvadev is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all beings and the idea that Lord Shiva pervades every aspect of existence. It inspires devotion, reverence, and awe towards the divine. Practitioners of the Sarvadev mantra seek inner peace, unity with the divine, and a deep understanding of the greatest truth, that is, Shiva as the omnipresent and all-abiding God.
